title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "C" Circuit High
plain: Your car uses two or more sensors to report gas pedal or throttle position. Sensor C's signal voltage is higher than it should ever be.
symptoms: Check engine light on, often with a reduced power warning
Engine stuck near idle or in limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Faulty electronic throttle body (sensor is built in)
Open ground wire or signal wire shorted to voltage
Loose or corroded connector at the throttle body or pedal

checks: Inspect the connectors at the throttle body and gas pedal for corrosion or loose pins
Check the sensor's 5-volt reference and ground at the connector
fix: Usually a new throttle body or gas pedal assembly, depending on which part holds the faulty sensor. Fix any wiring or connector damage first.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "C" Circuit Intermittent
plain: Your car uses two or more sensors to report gas pedal or throttle position. Sensor C's signal keeps cutting in and out.
symptoms: Check engine light on, often with a reduced power warning
Engine stuck near idle or in limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector at the throttle body or pedal
Chafed wiring that loses contact over bumps
Faulty electronic throttle body (sensor is built in)

checks: Inspect the connectors at the throttle body and gas pedal for corrosion or loose pins
Watch the sensor readings on a scan tool while wiggling the harness
fix: Usually a new throttle body or gas pedal assembly, depending on which part holds the faulty sensor. Fix any wiring or connector damage first.

title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control "A" Circuit Open
plain: Some turbo engines, mostly diesels, have a valve that can route intake air around the intercooler, for example to warm up faster. The computer sees an open (broken) circuit in the control for bypass valve A.
symptoms: Often no noticeable change in how it drives
Possibly reduced power or slower warm-up
checks: Inspect the bypass valve connector and wiring
Check the actuator's resistance and the computer's control signal
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new bypass valve actuator.

title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control "A" Circuit Low
plain: Some turbo engines, mostly diesels, have a valve that can route intake air around the intercooler, for example to warm up faster. The control circuit for bypass valve A reads lower than expected, often from a short to ground.
symptoms: Often no noticeable change in how it drives
Possibly reduced power or slower warm-up
checks: Inspect the bypass valve connector and wiring
Check the actuator's resistance and the computer's control signal
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new bypass valve actuator.

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit
plain: The computer switches the fuel pump on through a relay or driver module. It sees a problem in the circuit that does the switching.
symptoms: No fuel pump hum when the key is turned on

causes.name: Damaged wiring or corroded connector in the relay control circuit
Tripped fuel shutoff (inertia) switch on some Ford vehicles

checks: Listen for the fuel pump to hum for a couple of seconds with the key on
Check the fuel pump fuse and swap in a known-good relay
Inspect the relay control wiring, and the inertia switch if the vehicle has one
fix: Usually a new fuel pump relay or fuse, or a wiring repair. A driver module or computer fault is less common.

cost.job: Replace fuel pump relay and repair control circuit

drive: If the engine stalls or sputters, don't keep driving; the fuel pump could cut out in traffic and leave you stranded with heavy steering and brakes. If it starts and runs normally, keep trips short and go straight to a shop soon.
test_first: Check the fuel pump fuse, relay and inertia switch, listen for pump hum, and test power at the pump and the relay control wiring before replacing the pump, driver module or computer.

title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low
plain: The computer watches the power that goes out to the fuel pump. Here the voltage on the output side is lower than expected.
symptoms: Engine may crank but not start

causes.name: Worn fuel pump drawing too much current
Wiring to the pump shorted to ground
Corroded connector at the fuel pump
Faulty fuel pump relay or driver module

checks: Listen for the fuel pump to hum for a couple of seconds when the key is turned on
Inspect the fuel pump connector (often on top of the tank) and its wiring
Check fuel pump voltage and ground at the pump
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair at the tank, or a new fuel pump if it is worn out.

title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit High
plain: The computer watches the power that goes out to the fuel pump. Here the voltage on the output side is higher than expected.
symptoms: Engine may crank but not start

causes.name: Fuel pump wire shorted to power
Fuel pump unplugged or open circuit to the pump
Faulty fuel pump driver module or computer

checks: Listen for the fuel pump to hum for a couple of seconds when the key is turned on
Inspect the fuel pump connector (often on top of the tank) and its wiring
Check fuel pump voltage and ground at the pump
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair at the tank, or a new fuel pump if it is worn out.

title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Intermittent
plain: The computer watches the power that goes out to the fuel pump. Here the signal on the output side keeps cutting in and out.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger "A" Overboost Condition
plain: The turbo or supercharger made more boost pressure than the computer asked for. The computer usually cuts power to protect the engine.
symptoms: Check engine light on, often with limp mode
Sudden loss of power while accelerating
A surge of power just before the power cut

causes.name: Wastegate or wastegate actuator stuck closed
Faulty boost control solenoid or cracked vacuum hoses
Faulty boost pressure sensor reading too high

checks: Inspect boost control vacuum hoses and the wastegate linkage
Compare the boost sensor reading with barometric pressure with the engine off
Command the boost control solenoid and wastegate with a scan tool and watch them move
fix: Usually a new wastegate actuator or boost control solenoid, or freeing a sticking wastegate or turbo vanes. Replace the turbo only if it's confirmed stuck.

cost.job: Replace wastegate actuator or boost control solenoid

examples: Often seen on small turbo gas engines such as the GM 1.4L turbo in the Cruze, Trax and Encore
drive: Ease off and avoid hard acceleration. Too much boost can damage the engine, and the car may suddenly cut power. If you hear knocking or pinging, see smoke or lose power at speed, pull over safely and have it towed. Otherwise drive gently to a shop soon.
test_first: Check wastegate movement, the boost control solenoid and vacuum hoses, and compare the boost sensor with barometric pressure. Ask about any aftermarket tune before blaming the turbo.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: The boost sensor tells the computer how much pressure the turbo or supercharger is making. The computer sees a problem in this sensor's circuit.

causes.name: Damaged wiring between the sensor and computer

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring for damage or oil contamination
With the engine off, compare the boost sensor reading with barometric pressure
Check the boost hoses and intercooler pipes for leaks
fix: Usually a new boost pressure sensor or a wiring or connector repair. On diesels, cleaning a soot-clogged sensor or port sometimes fixes it.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The boost sensor tells the computer how much pressure the turbo or supercharger is making. Its reading doesn't make sense for how the engine is running.

causes.name: Leaking or cracked boost hose or intercooler pipe
Sensor port or hose clogged with oil or soot

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring for damage or oil contamination
With the engine off, compare the boost sensor reading with barometric pressure
Check the boost hoses and intercooler pipes for leaks
fix: Usually a new boost pressure sensor or a wiring or connector repair. On diesels, cleaning a soot-clogged sensor or port sometimes fixes it.
drive: You can usually drive gently to a shop soon, but expect reduced power or limp mode, so avoid highways and merging if power drops. If you hear knocking, see heavy smoke or the engine suddenly loses power, pull over and get it checked before driving on.
test_first: Compare the sensor reading with barometric pressure with the engine off, check for boost leaks and a clogged sensor port, and inspect the wiring before replacing the sensor.

fix: Usually a new boost pressure sensor or a wiring or connector repair. On diesels, cleaning a soot-clogged sensor or port sometimes fixes it.

test_first: Check the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal at the connector for an open or short to ground, and compare the engine-off reading with barometric pressure before replacing parts.

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor "A" Correlation
plain: The computer compares the intake manifold pressure sensor with boost sensor A. When the engine isn't making boost they should read about the same, and here they don't.

causes.name: Leaking, cracked or clogged sensor hoses or ports
Wiring or connector problem at either sensor

checks: With the engine off, compare both sensor readings with barometric pressure
Inspect both sensors' connectors, hoses and ports for leaks or clogging
fix: Usually replacing whichever sensor reads wrong when compared with barometric pressure.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Solenoid "A"

symptoms: Boost may surge or feel too strong at times
checks: Inspect the solenoid connector, wiring and vacuum hoses
Check the solenoid's resistance and command it with a scan tool
fix: Usually a new wastegate control solenoid or a wiring or hose repair.

checks: Inspect the bypass valve connector and wiring
Command the valve with a scan tool and watch whether it moves
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the bypass valve and actuator.

title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control "A" Stuck

title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: A position sensor tells the computer where the intercooler bypass valve is sitting. The computer sees a problem with the sensor signal.
symptoms: Often no noticeable change in how it drives

causes.name: Faulty bypass position sensor (often part of the valve assembly)
Short or open in the sensor reference or ground wire

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the sensor's reference voltage, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Usually a new bypass valve assembly with its sensor, or a wiring repair.
